conventions.convention: The coefficient bracket is [X,Y]^a=f^a_bc X^bY^c, without a factor of 1/2 in [c,c]. The ghost is odd of ghost number one; s is an odd left derivation with sAμ=Dμc, sc=−[c,c]/2 and sψ=−ρ(c)ψ. Jet prolongation commutes with total derivatives.

The finite-jet algebra consists of smooth coordinate coefficients and graded polynomials depending on finitely many formal jets; it contains only the minimal fields A, ψ and c. On horizontal forms, s(dxμ∧a)=−dxμ∧sa, so s anticommutes with d_H.

H^{g,p}(s|d_H) has cocycles sa+d_Hb=0 and boundaries sm+d_Hn. The spaces in form degree −1 are zero. Interpreting exact top forms as equal integrated functionals requires compact support or boundary conditions eliminating surface terms.

Antifields have parity ε_A+1 and ghost number −1−g_A. The canonical bracket uses right derivatives of its first argument and left derivatives of its second. With s=(S,−), the ordered antifield coupling is (−1)^ε_A Φ*_A s₀Φ^A; the optional nonminimal term is −c̄* b.

The reverse implication from Hamiltonian nilpotence to the classical master equation assumes no nonzero central element of ghost number one. This is proved for the finite canonical coordinate algebra and separately required for formal local-functional domains.
The SU(2) matrix basis is T_a=−iσ_a/2, with [T_a,T_b]=ε_ab^c T_c and ε¹₂₃=1.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, parity-preserving representation, graded-commutative finite-jet algebra and declared BRST formulas, s²=0 on the entire finite-jet algebra and sDμ=Dμs for each μ.

Defines the canonical odd field/antifield antibracket, its degree and shifted identities, the ordered minimal BV candidate S₀+∫Σ_A(−1)^ε_A Φ*_A s₀Φ^A, and the classical master equation, subject to the stated canonical-domain and local-functional qualifications.

For antifield-independent variations with the stated parities and ghost numbers, and even antifield-independent S₀ of ghost number zero, S=S₀+Σ_A(−1)^ε_A Φ*_A s₀Φ^A satisfies (S,Φ^A)=s₀Φ^A. The local version requires well-defined variational derivatives and integrations by parts with vanishing boundary term.

For even ghost-number-zero S_BV on the stated canonical algebra with no nonzero ghost-number-one center, s=(S_BV,−) is nilpotent if and only if (S_BV,S_BV)=0. The specified minimal local action satisfies that equation under the stated gauge-invariance, off-shell-closure, irreducibility and functional-domain hypotheses.

Defines H^{g,p}(s|d_H) as relative cocycles sa+d_Hb=0 modulo boundaries sm+d_Hn in the specified minimal finite-jet horizontal complex, with the degree-zero boundary convention and separate integration qualifications.

seams_checked.note: The page prerequisite provides geometric context. The BRST items independently state their local Lie-algebra and representation hypotheses; they do not infer a global bundle or group from these local data. Curvature normalization is compatible.

The citing items preserve the BRST and BV signs, explicitly define the extended field/antifield/nonminimal complex, and distinguish its restricted cohomology from minimal cohomology. Master-equation, domain, QAP and anomaly-cancellation assumptions remain explicit.

The Lorenz-gauge example uses the odd left-derivation sign correctly. It separately verifies nilpotence on the added antighost/auxiliary pair and uses the extended complex for its exactness conclusion.

The component BRST formulas and finite-jet nilpotence are cited with their Lie-algebra and representation hypotheses. Quantum Ward identities and regulator compatibility are separate assumptions, not consequences attributed to classical nilpotence.

The background complex preserves the component and horizontal-form signs, including sB=−d_Hη for the whole one-form. Restricted counterterm quotients are distinguished from unrestricted relative cohomology; counterterm shifts use precisely the stated relative boundaries.
